clue.text: Brilliant stroke of firm, having made a profit

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a business that is up has made money

explanation.surface: A firm pulls off a masterstroke and turns a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup is a sudden, highly successful move, a masterstroke.

clue.text: Rotten Row

explanation.surface: Rotten Row is the riding track in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a famous bridle path in Hyde Park, London; split apart, the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul or rotten, and a rank is also a row, as of soldiers or taxis.

clue.text: Fail to meet girl

explanation.surface: Someone fails to turn up for a date with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss someone is to fail to meet them, and Miss is the title of an unmarried girl or young woman.

clue.text: Mad Hatter point to Cambridge, for example?

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters have gone crazy and are jumbled

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice points the way to the university town of Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge here is not the university city but the Cambridge Theatre in London's West End, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cambridge is a London playhouse, an example of a venue for drama.

clue.text: Style of guitar playing needing courage and audacity

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is British slang for cheek or audacity

explanation.surface: A guitar technique is said to demand nerve and daring.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang both bottle and neck mean nerve; the guitar style uses a glass bottle neck slid along the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottleneck is a slide-guitar style played with a glass tube or bottle neck on the fingers.

clue.text: One makes a splash in do, as on ship at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone causes a splash at a party held on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' reworks DO AS ON SHIP; 'do' looks like a verb but is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A soda siphon squirts fizzy water, splashing it into a drink.

clue.text: Infamous four in sea-battle

indicators.note: a battle is a melee in which everything is thrown about, so the letters fight their way into a new order

explanation.surface: Four ships disgrace themselves in a naval engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-battle' looks like one compound noun, but 'sea' is part of the fodder FOUR IN SEA and 'battle' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or villainous, as an infamous deed is.

clue.text: Power-group scheme

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
a lot is a group or batch of things

explanation.surface: A power bloc hatches a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan or conspiracy.

clue.text: For a medley from Truro, I pop out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or knocked out of place

explanation.surface: Someone pops out of Truro, the Cornish town, to fetch a mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Truro is the county town of Cornwall; 'out' rearranges TRURO I POP.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixed collection, like a musical medley.

clue.text: Fishpole, something plain to see

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a long stick or pole

explanation.surface: A fishing pole is obvious to anyone looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'plain as a pikestaff' makes the old spear handle the proverbial example of obviousness.

clue.text: Letter written in tea-break

indicators.note: break suggests the word tea is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A letter is written during a tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea-break' looks like an interval, but 'break' is the anagram signal working on TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: To carry child needs energy

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Carrying a little one takes a lot of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to lug or carry, especially something heavy.

clue.text: The means of Cleopatra's passing?

parts.note: Cleopatra is said to have died by letting a venomous snake bite her

explanation.surface: How did the Egyptian queen die?
explanation.definitionFit: Legend has Cleopatra killing herself with the bite of a small Egyptian viper.

clue.text: Rate of exchange more certain to find the fund-manager

indicators.note: exchange means the letters of rate swap places with one another

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A good exchange rate makes it more likely someone finds a fund-manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate of exchange' looks like finance, but 'of exchange' rearranges RATE to TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer looks after an organisation's money, its funds.

clue.text: Slender and majestic in pensive mood

parts.note: thin means slender
kingly means regal or majestic

explanation.surface: A slim and regal figure appears lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinkingly means thoughtfully, as one would act when pensive.

clue.text: Cafe in which teatime's arranged about noon

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the other letter
arranged means the letters are reordered

parts.note: the word teatime with its 's taken as an S

explanation.surface: A cafe where afternoon tea is set up around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' jumbles TEATIMES, with the S of 'teatime's' counted, and 'about' wraps it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or bistro.

clue.text: Safe job a bit of a fiddle?

parts.note: sound means secure or safe
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A secure job turns out to be a bit of a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a swindle but is the violin; the soundpost is a small dowel inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundpost is the small wooden prop inside a violin linking front and back.

clue.text: University in which none are gated?

definitions.text: University in which none are gated?

parts.words: University in which none are gated?
parts.note: gating is confining students to college; a university with no barriers or entry requirements is the distance-learning one

explanation.surface: Which university never confines its students?
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university, with no entry requirements; to be 'gated' is to be confined to college as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no gates or barriers is accessible to all, unrestricted.

clue.text: Maximum single holding of US dollars?

definitions.text: Maximum single holding of US dollars?

parts.words: Maximum single holding of US dollars?
parts.note: the most cash one hand can grasp, recalling the Western film A ... of Dollars

explanation.surface: What is the most US currency one investor may hold?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' looks financial but means grasping in the hand; the phrase echoes the Clint Eastwood Western.
explanation.definitionFit: A handful clenched in the hand is as much as a single hand can hold.

clue.text: Hunts making tracks

explanation.surface: Hunting parties set off across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To course is to chase hares with hounds, and also to run or flow swiftly along.

clue.text: Strange articles bric-a brac around university

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: curios are knick-knacks or bric-a-brac

explanation.surface: Odd knick-knacks lie scattered about a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious means odd or peculiar.

clue.text: Second Kipling hero is separate

parts.note: Kim is the title character of Rudyard Kipling's novel

explanation.surface: Another hero from Kipling stands apart from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim milk is to separate the cream from it.

clue.text: Piece of chicken for battering?

explanation.surface: Chicken pieces are coated before frying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battering' suggests coating in batter, but the second sense is a stick for beating a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumstick is the lower leg of a fowl and also the stick a percussionist beats with.

clue.text: Pot for a beverage

explanation.surface: A pot is brewed for drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like a teapot, but it is old slang for marijuana, also once called tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea was period slang for cannabis, and is also the everyday hot drink.

clue.text: I am contracted to play quietly with mischievous child

parts.note: I am shortened gives I'm
p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone is hired to perform softly for a naughty youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a little devil, a playfully naughty child.

clue.text: Soon lacking individual characteristics, in short

explanation.surface: Before long someone will be stripped of all personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is old-fashioned for shortly, and is also the abbreviation for anonymous, faceless.

clue.text: Rifle ammo ordered to the French standard

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Rifle ammunition is requisitioned to French army specifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests a specification, but means a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red banner of the early kings of France.

clue.text: Cool off engine

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: Let a hot motor cool down.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is short for locomotive, a railway engine.

clue.text: Encounter me and French

parts.note: et is French for and

explanation.surface: Run into me and a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone is to come across them.

clue.text: Bird sitting in another nest

indicators.note: sitting in means the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A bird is sitting in another bird's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle.

clue.text: Tone-lowering character in apartment

explanation.surface: A rowdy tenant brings down the tone of the apartment block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tone-lowering' suggests vulgarity, but it is the musical sign that drops a note a semitone.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat sign lowers a note by a semitone, and a flat is also a set of rooms on one floor.

clue.text: Exciting turn chosen for these clubs?

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrilling performance is picked for these nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests nightspots but means the cudgels police carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Truncheons are short heavy sticks used as weapons, clubs.
